l1: What VPN tunnel type is in use — SSTP (TCP 443), IKEv2 (UDP 500/4500), L2TP/IPsec (UDP 1701/500/4500), or Always On VPN (AOVPN) Device/User Tunnel? Run: Get-VpnConnection | Select Name,TunnelType,ServerAddress

What Windows version is the VPN client, and what OS is the VPN server (Windows Server RRAS, Azure VPN Gateway, or third-party appliance)? Run client: [System.Environment]::OSVersion.Version; server: Get-ComputerInfo | Select OsName,OsVersion
Is this a Remote Access VPN (per-user dial-in) or a Site-to-Site (gateway-to-gateway) IPsec tunnel? Run on RRAS: Get-RemoteAccessVpnServerConfiguration | Select VpnType

What is the exact error code displayed at connection time? (Error 691, 812, 809, 789, 13801, 868, 800, 619, 721) Check Event Viewer: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -ProviderName RasClient -MaxEvents 5 | Format-List

Is the failure at authentication (credentials/certificate rejected), tunnel establishment (IKE/IPsec phase failure), or post-connect (tunnel up but no access to resources)? Test: ping internal resource, route print, Test-NetConnection

Is this affecting all VPN users or specific users, devices, or locations (e.g., only from behind certain NATs)? Run on NPS: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Id 6273 -MaxEvents 20 | Group-Object -Property Message

What authentication method is configured — NPS/RADIUS with PEAP or EAP-TLS, certificate-only (IKEv2), PAP, MS-CHAPv2, or EAP-MS-CHAPv2? Run: Get-VpnConnection | Select AuthenticationMethod; NPS: netsh nps show np

When did the issue start — server certificate expiry, NPS configuration change, firewall rule change, Windows Update, or new client device/OS? Check cert: certutil -store My; check NPS: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Id 6273 | Select TimeCreated
Can the VPN client reach the VPN server public IP or FQDN from the internet before attempting to connect? Run: Test-NetConnection <VPN IP> -Port 443; Test-NetConnection <VPN IP> -Port 500
l2: For IKEv2: what machine certificate and user certificate are in use — are they valid, not expired, issued by the correct CA, and contain the required EKUs (Server Authentication, Client Authentication, IP Security IKE Intermediate)? Run: certutil -store My; certutil -store -machine My; check EKU: certutil -v -store My <thumbprint>

For SSTP: is the VPN server SSL certificate trusted by the client — is the full certificate chain present, the root CA trusted, and the certificate CN/SAN matching the server FQDN/IP? Run: netsh http show sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443; certutil -verify <certfile>

For Always On VPN: is this the Device Tunnel (machine cert, connects before logon) or User Tunnel (user cert or MSCHAPv2, connects at user logon)? What is the AOVPN profile source (Intune, SCCM, manual)? Run: Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection; Get-VpnConnection; Get-MdmVpnConnectionProfile

Is split tunneling configured — what specific routes are pushed to the VPN client via RRAS static routes or AOVPN VPNv2 profile RouteList? Run: Get-VpnConnectionRoute -ConnectionName <name>; route print; Get-RemoteAccessRoutingDomain

What NPS Connection Request Policy and Network Policy are matching VPN authentication — what conditions, constraints, and RADIUS attributes are configured? Run: netsh nps show crp; netsh nps show np; netsh nps show exportedxml

Are all required firewall rules and NAT translations in place — IKEv2 (UDP 500, UDP 4500), SSTP (TCP 443), L2TP (UDP 1701, UDP 500, UDP 4500, ESP protocol 50)? Run: Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound | Where DisplayName -like '*VPN*'; Get-NetFirewallPortFilter

Is NAT Traversal (NAT-T) enabled on the RRAS server for IKEv2 and L2TP clients connecting from behind NAT? Run: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RemoteAccess\Parameters\Ikev2' -Name NatTraversalMode

What DNS servers and DNS suffixes are pushed to VPN clients post-connection — are they reachable through the VPN tunnel? Are NRPT rules configured for the VPN domain suffix? Run: ipconfig /all; Get-DnsClientNrptRule; Get-VpnConnection | Select DnsSuffix

For AOVPN: is the XML VPN profile correctly structured per Microsoft's AOVPN CSP (VPNv2 Profile) specification — are there syntax errors in the profile XML? Run: Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection | ConvertTo-Json; Validate XML: [System.Xml.XmlDocument]::Load('profile.xml')

l1: What is the exact 4-digit or 5-digit Windows VPN error code? (visible in the VPN connection UI or Event Viewer > System — Source: RasClient, Event ID 20227 or 20228) Run: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -ProviderName RasClient -MaxEvents 10 | Where Id -in (20227,20228) | Format-List TimeCreated,Message

Run 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <VPN server FQDN> -Port 443' (SSTP) or '-Port 500' (IKEv2) — is the server reachable from the client network? For UDP ports, use: portqry -n <VPN IP> -e 500 -p udp; portqry -n <VPN IP> -e 4500 -p udp

On the VPN server: review System event log — filter on source 'RemoteAccess' or 'RasServer' — note Event IDs 20063 (auth failure), 20249 (IPsec negotiation failure). Run: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -ProviderName RemoteAccess -MaxEvents 20 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message
Run 'Get-Service RemoteAccess | Select Name,Status,StartType' on the RRAS server. Also check: Get-Service RasMan,Get-Service RemoteRegistry,Get-Service WinHttpAutoProxySvc
On NPS: filter Security event log for Event ID 6273 — note Reason Code and username/device. Run: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Id 6273 -MaxEvents 10 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message

Run 'ipconfig /all' on the client before and after VPN connection — compare DNS servers, default gateway, and new VPN adapter routes. Run: Get-NetIPConfiguration; Get-NetRoute | Where DestinationPrefix -notlike '127.0.0.0/8'

Can the same user connect from a different client machine — isolates machine-specific (cert, profile) vs. user-specific (credentials, account) issues? Test with second client and compare: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -ProviderName RasClient -MaxEvents 20
l2: On the RRAS server: enable PPP tracing — 'netsh ras set tracing * enabled' — reproduce — collect C:\Windows\tracing\ppp*.log — disable: 'netsh ras set tracing * disabled'. Also enable IKE tracing: netsh ras set tracing IKEV2 enabled

Run 'Get-VpnConnection | Select Name,ServerAddress,TunnelType,AuthenticationMethod,EncryptionLevel,SplitTunneling,DnsSuffix' — share all VPN connection profiles. For AOVPN: Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection | Select Name,ServerAddress,TunnelType,ConnectionStatus

For IKEv2: 'netsh ike show certmap' — confirm the machine certificate is mapped to the IKEv2 interface for authentication. Also run: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select Subject,Issuer,NotBefore,NotAfter,EnhancedKeyUsageList
Run 'Get-VpnServerConfiguration' on the RRAS server — share TunnelType, IPv4AddressRange, IPv4DnsServer, and EncryptionType. Run: Get-RemoteAccessVpnServerConfiguration | Select *

For AOVPN: export Device Tunnel profile — 'Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection | ConvertTo-Json | Out-File C:\aovpn_device_tunnel.json'. Check profile deployment: Get-MdmVpnConnectionProfile; For Intune: MDMDiagnosticsTool.exe -out C:\MDMLogs\

Run 'netsh ras show authtype > C:\ras_authtype.txt' and 'netsh ras show protocol > C:\ras_protocols.txt' on RRAS server. Also: netsh ras show user; netsh ras show link; netsh ras show registeredserver

Capture IKE trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-IKEEXT level=5 tracefile=C:\ike_trace.etl' — reproduce — stop. Also capture RasMan: netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-RasMan level=5 tracefile=C:\rasman_trace.etl
For SSTP: run 'netsh http show sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443' — confirm certhash matches the expected VPN server certificate thumbprint. Verify cert chain: certutil -verify -urlfetch <certfile>
Run 'netsh ipsec dynamic show all > C:\ipsec_dynamic_state.txt' on both client and server for IPsec/L2TP phase analysis. Also: Get-NetIPsecMainModeSA; Get-NetIPsecQuickModeSA
Check RRAS server certificate validity: certutil -store My; verify EKU includes Server Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1) for SSTP, IP Security IKE Intermediate (1.3.6.1.5.5.8.2.2) for IKEv2
Test NPS RADIUS connectivity: Test-NetConnection <NPS server> -Port 1812; Test-NetConnection <NPS server> -Port 1813; Check NPS shared secret: netsh nps show exportedxml

l1: Error 691 (auth failed): verify username/password, check AD account not locked, and confirm NPS Network Policy matches VPN connection request. Run: Get-ADUser <username> -Properties Enabled,LockedOut,PasswordExpired; Unlock-ADAccount if needed

Error 812 (connection prevented by policy): NPS is rejecting — check Event 6273 Reason Code — verify NPS policy conditions and that the user account has Allow Access. Run: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Id 6273 -MaxEvents 5 | Format-List; Get-ADUser <user> -Properties msNPAllowDialin

Error 809 (IKEv2 network connection could not be established): firewall is blocking UDP 500 or 4500 — verify all NATs and firewalls permit these ports bidirectionally. Run: Test-NetConnection <VPN IP> -Port 500; Test-NetConnection <VPN IP> -Port 4500; Check firewall: Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound | Where DisplayName -like '*IKE*'

Error 789 (L2TP security negotiation failed): machine certificate missing or wrong for L2TP/IPsec, or IPsec policy mismatch — switch to pre-shared key for testing, then resolve cert issue. Run: certutil -store -machine My; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\PolicyAgent' -Name AssumeUDPEncapsulationContextOnSendScope -Value 2

Error 13801 (IKEv2 authentication credentials unacceptable): machine cert missing, expired, wrong CA, or missing IKE EKU — re-enroll from the correct certificate template. Run: certutil -store -machine My; Verify EKU includes 1.3.6.1.5.5.8.2.2; Re-enroll: certreq -new -accept vpn_machine_cert.inf

Error 868 (name could not be resolved): DNS cannot resolve the VPN server FQDN — test with IP address directly; if that works, DNS is the issue. Run: Resolve-DnsName <VPN FQDN>; Test-NetConnection <VPN IP> -Port 443; Check DNS suffix search list: Get-DnsClientGlobalSetting
Restart RRAS: 'Restart-Service RemoteAccess' — wait 60-90 seconds for all interfaces to initialize — retest. Also restart dependent services: Restart-Service RasMan; Restart-Service RemoteRegistry
Error 720 (no PPP control protocols configured): missing or corrupted WAN miniport drivers — reinstall WAN miniports via Device Manager or run: netcfg -d (reset network stack - requires reboot)
l2: For SSTP certificate binding: rebind the correct cert — 'netsh http add sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443 certhash=<thumbprint> appid={ba195980-cd49-458b-9e23-c84ee0adcd75}'. Verify binding: netsh http show sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443; If binding fails, check SSL cert: certutil -store My; Ensure CN/SAN matches VPN server FQDN

For IKEv2 machine cert not being offered: verify cert is in LocalMachine\My store, contains IP Security IKE Intermediate EKU (OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.8.2.2) or Server Authentication EKU, and the CN/SAN matches the RRAS server FQDN. Run: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select Subject,Issuer,NotBefore,NotAfter,EnhancedKeyUsageList; Test: netsh ike show certmap

For AOVPN Device Tunnel not connecting: confirm client machine is domain-joined, Device Tunnel profile deployed as AllUserConnection, machine cert valid, and the profile NativeProtocol = IKEv2 only. Run: Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection; Get-ComputerInfo | Select CsPartOfDomain; Check cert: certutil -store -machine My; For Intune: MDMDiagnosticsTool.exe -out C:\MDMLogs\

For split tunnel route issues: 'Get-VpnConnectionRoute -ConnectionName <name>' — confirm all corporate subnets are in IncludeRoutes list; remove conflicting ExcludeRoutes. Run: Get-VpnConnectionRoute -ConnectionName <name>; Set-VpnConnectionRoute -ConnectionName <name> -DestinationPrefix <subnet> -PassThru; Check RRAS static routes: Get-RemoteAccessRoutingDomain

For DNS not resolving over VPN: confirm correct DNS servers are pushed — 'Get-VpnConnection | Select DnsSuffix,SplitTunneling' — and NRPT rules include the VPN domain suffix: 'Get-DnsClientNrptRule'. Run: Set-VpnConnection -Name <name> -DnsSuffix <domain> -DnsServer <DNS IP>; Add-DnsClientNrptRule -Namespace <domain> -NameServers <DNS IP>

For IKEv2 NAT-T failure (client behind NAT): enable NAT-T on RRAS — 'Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RemoteAccess\Parameters\Ikev2" -Name NatTraversalMode -Value 2' — reboot RRAS. Verify: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RemoteAccess\Parameters\Ikev2' -Name NatTraversalMode

Analyze IKE ETL trace: look for IKE_AUTH failure notifications: NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN (cipher suite mismatch), TS_UNACCEPTABLE (traffic selector mismatch), AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Use tracerpt or Message Analyzer to parse C:\ike_trace.etl; Search for 'FAILED' and error codes

For Always On VPN with Intune: run 'MDMDiagnosticsTool.exe -out C:\MDMLogs\' — review MDMDiagReport.xml for VPN profile deployment errors. Check: MDM Logs > Enterprise > VPNv2; Verify profile deployment in Intune portal; Check enrollment status: dsregcmd /status

For NPS RADIUS authentication issues: verify RADIUS client is registered on NPS server with correct shared secret. Run: netsh nps show client; Test RADIUS: Test-NetConnection <NPS IP> -Port 1812; Check NPS logs: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Id 6272,6273 -MaxEvents 20

For certificate chain trust issues: ensure full certificate chain is present on client, root CA is in Trusted Root store, intermediate CAs in Intermediate store. Run: certutil -store Root; certutil -store CA; Verify chain: certutil -verify -urlfetch <certfile>; Export chain: certutil -store My <thumbprint>

For L2TP/IPsec pre-shared key mismatch: verify same PSK configured on RRAS server and client. Run on RRAS: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RasMan\Parameters' -Name 'ProhibitIpSec'; Set PSK: Set-VpnServerConfiguration -RadiusSecret <secret> (if using RADIUS) or configure in RRAS console

For VPN connection drops after idle timeout: adjust RRAS idle timeout settings. Run: Set-RemoteAccessVpnServerConfiguration -IdleDisconnectMinutes <minutes>; Check client timeout: Get-VpnConnection | Select IdleDisconnectSeconds; Set: Set-VpnConnection -Name <name> -IdleDisconnectSeconds <seconds>

l1: Export System event log: 'wevtutil epl System C:\System_Events_VPN.evtx'. Also export Application log: wevtutil epl Application C:\App_Events_VPN.evtx; Filter for VPN events: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -ProviderName RasClient,RemoteAccess -MaxEvents 100 | Export-Csv C:\VPN_System_Events.csv

Run 'Get-VpnConnection | Out-File C:\vpn_client_connections.txt'. Also export full config: Get-VpnConnection | Select * | Export-Csv C:\vpn_connections_full.csv; For AOVPN: Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection | Select * | Export-Csv C:\aovpn_connections.csv

Run 'ipconfig /all > C:\ipconfig_before_vpn.txt' (before attempt); 'ipconfig /all > C:\ipconfig_after_vpn.txt' (after attempt). Also capture: Get-NetIPConfiguration | Out-File C:\netconfig_before.txt; Get-NetIPConfiguration | Out-File C:\netconfig_after.txt; Get-NetRoute | Out-File C:\routes_before.txt; Get-NetRoute | Out-File C:\routes_after.txt

On NPS: export Security event log: 'wevtutil epl Security C:\NPS_Security_Events.evtx'. Filter for RADIUS events: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Id 6272,6273,6278,6280 -MaxEvents 100 | Export-Csv C:\NPS_RADIUS_Events.csv

Collect RRAS server configuration: Get-RemoteAccessVpnServerConfiguration | Out-File C:\rras_vpn_config.txt; Get-RemoteAccessRoutingDomain | Out-File C:\rras_routing_domains.txt; Get-RemoteAccessRadiusConfiguration | Out-File C:\rras_radius_config.txt

Export NPS configuration: netsh nps show exportedxml > C:
ps_config.xml; netsh nps show crp > C:
ps_connection_request_policies.txt; netsh nps show np > C:
ps_network_policies.txt
l2: Enable RRAS PPP tracing: 'netsh ras set tracing * enabled' — reproduce — collect C:\Windows\tracing\ppp*.log — disable: 'netsh ras set tracing * disabled'. Also enable specific protocols: netsh ras set tracing IKEV2 enabled; netsh ras set tracing L2TP enabled; netsh ras set tracing SSTP enabled

Capture IKE trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-IKEEXT level=5 tracefile=C:\ike_ikeext.etl' — reproduce — stop. Also capture: netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-RasMan level=5 tracefile=C:\rasman_trace.etl; netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-RemoteAccess level=5 tracefile=C:\remoteaccess_trace.etl

Run 'Get-VpnServerConfiguration | Out-File C:\rras_vpn_server_config.txt' on the RRAS server. Also: Get-VpnServerConfiguration | Select * | Export-Csv C:\rras_vpn_config.csv; Get-RemoteAccessAccounting | Out-File C:\rras_accounting.txt

Run 'netsh ras show authtype > C:\ras_authtype.txt' and 'netsh ras show protocol > C:\ras_protocol.txt'. Also: netsh ras show user > C:\ras_users.txt; netsh ras show link > C:\ras_link.txt; netsh ras show registeredserver > C:\ras_registered_server.txt; netsh ras show aaa > C:\ras_aaa.txt

Run 'netsh ipsec dynamic show all > C:\ipsec_dynamic.txt' on both client and RRAS server. Also: Get-NetIPsecMainModeSA | Out-File C:\ipsec_mainmode_sa.txt; Get-NetIPsecQuickModeSA | Out-File C:\ipsec_quickmode_sa.txt; Get-NetIPsecPhase1AuthSet | Out-File C:\ipsec_phase1_auth.txt

Export AOVPN profiles: 'Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection | ConvertTo-Json | Out-File C:\aovpn_device.json'. Also export registry: reg export HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RemoteAccess\Parameters\Vpn C:\vpn_registry.reg; For Intune: MDMDiagnosticsTool.exe -out C:\MDMLogs\

Run 'certutil -store My > C:\rras_server_certs.txt' on the RRAS server. Also: certutil -store -machine My > C:\rras_machine_certs.txt; certutil -store Root > C:\root_certs.txt; certutil -store CA > C:\intermediate_certs.txt; Export specific cert: certutil -store My <thumbprint> > C:\vpn_cert_details.txt
Collect NPS verbose trace: 'netsh nps set tracing mode=all' — reproduce — disable — collect C:\Windows\tracing\nps.log. Also enable SQL logging if configured: netsh nps set logging mode=enable

TSS full data collection: '.\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_VPN' — run on the affected VPN client, reproduce the connection failure, stop when prompted. Also collect: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 500 | Export-Csv C:\tss_system.csv; Get-WinEvent -LogName Application -MaxEvents 500 | Export-Csv C:\tss_app.csv

Collect DNS configuration: Get-DnsClientServerAddress | Out-File C:\dns_client_servers.txt; Get-DnsClientNrptRule | Out-File C:\dns_nrpt_rules.txt; Get-DnsClientCache | Out-File C:\dns_cache.txt; Get-DnsClientGlobalSetting | Out-File C:\dns_global_settings.txt

Collect firewall rules: Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound | Where DisplayName -like '*VPN*' | Export-Csv C:\firewall_inbound_vpn.csv; Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Outbound | Where DisplayName -like '*VPN*' | Export-Csv C:\firewall_outbound_vpn.csv; Get-NetFirewallPortFilter | Export-Csv C:\firewall_ports.csv

Collect network adapter info: Get-NetAdapter | Select Name,InterfaceDescription,Status,LinkSpeed | Out-File C:
et_adapters.txt; Get-NetIPInterface | Out-File C:
et_ipinterface.txt; Get-NetIPv4Protocol | Out-File C:
et_ipv4_protocol.txt; Get-NetIPv6Protocol | Out-File C:
et_ipv6_protocol.txt

Collect registry keys for VPN: reg export HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RasMan C:\rasman_registry.reg; reg export HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\PolicyAgent C:\policyagent_registry.reg; reg export HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce C:\runonce_registry.reg

error_691_812.title: VPN Error 691 or 812 — authentication rejected by NPS or credentials invalid

steps.action: Note exact error code: 691 = auth failed at PPP level; 812 = NPS policy rejected. Check Event Viewer: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -ProviderName RasClient -MaxEvents 5 | Format-List
steps.expect: Error code determines whether issue is credentials (691) or NPS policy (812)

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security | Where Id -eq 6273 on NPS | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Reason Code and username — confirms NPS is receiving and rejecting the request. Reason Code 16 = authentication failed, 64 = connection attempt not allowed

steps.action: Test-NetConnection <NPS server> -Port 1812 and -Port 1813 from RRAS server
steps.expect: RADIUS ports accessible — confirms RRAS can reach NPS server

steps.action: Get-ADUser <username> -Properties Enabled,LockedOut,PasswordExpired,AccountLockoutTime | Select *
steps.expect: Account enabled, not locked, password not expired. If locked, note lockout time

steps.action: Get-ADUser <username> -Properties msNPAllowDialin | Select msNPAllowDialin
steps.expect: Value should be $null (policy-controlled) or $true — if $false, user is always denied regardless of NPS policy

steps.action: netsh nps show np — check Network Policy conditions and order. Look for NAS-Port-Type, Windows Groups, Tunnel-Type conditions
steps.expect: A policy exists that matches VPN connection type and user group. Policy order matters — first matching policy wins

steps.action: netsh nps show crp — check Connection Request Policy for RADIUS client validation
steps.expect: RRAS server is registered as RADIUS client with correct shared secret

steps.action: Unlock-ADAccount -Identity <user> if locked. Check lockout policy: net accounts /lockoutthreshold
steps.expect: Account unlocked — retry VPN connection. If recurring lockouts, investigate incorrect credentials or brute force

steps.action: Set-ADUser <user> -Clear msNPAllowDialin if value is $false. Or Set-ADUser <user> -Replace @{msNPAllowDialin=$true}
steps.expect: Dial-in permission set to policy-controlled ($null) or explicitly allowed ($true) — NPS policy now governs access

steps.action: Fix NPS Network Policy conditions to match VPN request attributes. Check NAS-Port-Type (Virtual), Windows Groups, Tunnel-Type (IKEv2/SSTP/L2TP). Ensure Grant Remote Access Permission is checked
steps.expect: Policy matches — authentication succeeds. Use netsh nps show np to verify policy includes correct conditions

steps.action: Verify RADIUS shared secret matches between RRAS and NPS. On RRAS: Get-RemoteAccessRadiusConfiguration. On NPS: netsh nps show client
steps.expect: Shared secret identical on both servers. Mismatch causes authentication failure

steps.action: Retry VPN connection from client
steps.expect: Connects successfully — no error 691 or 812. Check connection status: Get-VpnConnection | Select Name,ConnectionStatus

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security | Where Id -eq 6272 on NPS | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Event 6272 = authentication succeeded. User authenticated and connected to VPN

steps.action: Get-RemoteAccessConnectionStatistics on RRAS server | Select ActiveConnections
steps.expect: Active connection count incremented — confirms successful VPN session

error_809_ikev2.title: VPN Error 809 — IKEv2 tunnel cannot be established due to network/firewall issues

steps.action: Test-NetConnection <VPN server FQDN> -Port 500. For accurate UDP test: portqry -n <VPN IP> -e 500 -p udp
steps.expect: UDP 500 open and reachable. If blocked, IKEv2 SA negotiation fails

steps.action: Test-NetConnection <VPN server FQDN> -Port 4500. Use: portqry -n <VPN IP> -e 4500 -p udp
steps.expect: UDP 4500 open and reachable. Required for NAT-T when client is behind NAT device

steps.action: Get-Service RemoteAccess on RRAS server | Select Name,Status,StartType
steps.expect: Status: Running. If stopped, start with Start-Service RemoteAccess

steps.action: Check if client is behind NAT: ipconfig /all and compare public IP via external service
steps.expect: If client behind NAT, NAT-T (UDP 4500) must be enabled on RRAS server

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName System | Where ProviderName -eq 'RemoteAccess' | Select -First 5 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message
steps.expect: Event 20249 = IPsec negotiation failure — note the specific IKE error code. Check for NAT-T related errors

steps.action: netsh ike show certmap on RRAS server. Verify machine certificate is bound to IKEv2
steps.expect: Machine certificate mapped to IKEv2 interface — if missing, IKEv2 has no cert to offer for authentication

steps.action: Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound | Where DisplayName -like '*IKE*' | Select DisplayName,Enabled,Action
steps.expect: IKEv2 firewall rules enabled and allowing inbound UDP 500 and 4500

steps.action: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RemoteAccess\Parameters\Ikev2' -Name NatTraversalMode
steps.expect: Value 2 = NAT-T enabled (default for clients behind NAT). Value 0 = disabled, Value 1 = automatic

steps.action: Open UDP 500 and UDP 4500 inbound on RRAS server Windows Firewall. Run: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'IKEv2 Inbound' -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 500,4500 -Action Allow
steps.expect: IKEv2 negotiation traffic now reaches RRAS. Verify with Get-NetFirewallRule

steps.action: Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RemoteAccess\Parameters\Ikev2' -Name NatTraversalMode -Value 2. Restart RRAS: Restart-Service RemoteAccess
steps.expect: NAT-T forced on RRAS — required for clients behind NAT. Registry change requires RRAS restart

steps.action: Ensure perimeter firewall/network device allows UDP 500 and 4500 to RRAS server public IP. Check edge firewall logs for dropped packets
steps.expect: Perimeter firewall permits IKEv2 traffic. No packet drops visible in firewall logs

steps.action: If machine certificate issue: verify cert in LocalMachine\My store with IP Security IKE Intermediate EKU (1.3.6.1.5.5.8.2.2). Run: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select Subject,EnhancedKeyUsageList
steps.expect: Valid machine certificate with correct EKU present. Re-enroll if missing or expired

steps.action: Retry VPN connection from client
steps.expect: IKEv2 tunnel establishes — no error 809. Check: Get-VpnConnection | Select Name,ConnectionStatus

steps.action: Get-RemoteAccessConnectionStatistics on RRAS server | Select ActiveConnections
steps.expect: Active connection count incremented — confirms successful IKEv2 session

steps.action: Verify IKEv2 SA established: Get-NetIPsecMainModeSA | Where RemoteAddress -eq '<client IP>'
steps.expect: IPsec Main Mode SA visible — confirms IKE phase 1 negotiation successful

aovpn_device_tunnel.title: Always On VPN Device Tunnel not connecting — pre-logon machine authentication failure

steps.action: Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection | Select Name,ServerAddress,TunnelType,ConnectionStatus,AllUserConnection
steps.expect: Device Tunnel profile present with TunnelType: IKEv2 and AllUserConnection: True

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName System | Where ProviderName -eq 'RasClient' | Select -First 5 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message
steps.expect: Event 20227 or 20228 = VPN connection failed — note error code. Common: 13801 (cert issue), 809 (network)

steps.action: Check if profile deployed via MDM: Get-MdmVpnConnectionProfile. Or check registry: Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\DeviceConnect\VPNProfiles'
steps.expect: Profile visible in MDM/registry — confirms deployment mechanism

steps.action: certutil -store -machine My | findstr 'Subject'
steps.expect: Machine cert present — Device Tunnel requires machine cert not user cert. Check CN matches machine name

steps.action: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select Subject,Issuer,NotBefore,NotAfter,EnhancedKeyUsageList
steps.expect: Machine cert valid (not expired), has Client Authentication EKU (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1) and IP Security IKE Intermediate (1.3.6.1.5.5.8.2.2)

steps.action: Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection | ConvertTo-Json | Out-File C:\aovpn_profile.json
steps.expect: Profile deployed as AllUserConnection — if missing, Intune or SCCM deployment failed. Check profile NativeProtocol = IKEv2

steps.action: Get-ComputerInfo | Select CsPartOfDomain,CsDomain,CsWorkgroup
steps.expect: Machine domain-joined. Device Tunnel requires domain join for machine certificate auto-enrollment

steps.action: dsregcmd /status — check Azure AD/Domain join status
steps.expect: Domain Joined: Yes. If Workplace Joined or Azure AD only, machine cert enrollment may fail

steps.action: Re-enroll machine cert: certlm.msc > Personal > Request New Certificate. Select VPN machine certificate template with correct EKUs
steps.expect: Valid machine cert with Client Authentication and IP Security IKE Intermediate EKU. Verify in LocalMachine\My store

steps.action: MDMDiagnosticsTool.exe -out C:\MDMLogs\ if deployed via Intune. Review MDMDiagReport.xml for VPN profile deployment errors
steps.expect: MDMDiagReport.xml shows VPN profile deployment status and any CSP errors. Check Enterprise > VPNv2 section

steps.action: If SCCM deployed: check Configuration Manager console for VPN profile deployment status. Check client logs: C:\Windows\CCM\Logs\CCMVPN.log
steps.expect: Profile deployed successfully. Check for deployment errors in SCCM logs

steps.action: Restart-Service RasMan. Also restart: Restart-Service RemoteAccess if on RRAS server
steps.expect: Remote Access Connection Manager restarted — Device Tunnel re-attempts connection

steps.action: If profile XML issue: validate XML syntax per Microsoft AOVPN CSP specification. Check VPNv2 ProfileXML structure: NativeProtocol, AuthenticationMethod, ServerList
steps.expect: XML well-formed and compliant with AOVPN CSP. Use [System.Xml.XmlDocument]::Load() to validate

steps.action: Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection | Select Name,ConnectionStatus
steps.expect: ConnectionStatus: Connected. Device Tunnel should connect at boot before user logon

steps.action: Test-NetConnection <internal resource> from client before user logon (at lock screen or via scheduled task)
steps.expect: Internal resource reachable via Device Tunnel — confirms pre-logon connectivity

steps.action: Check Device Tunnel persistence: reboot client and verify auto-connects. Get-VpnConnection -AllUserConnection after reboot
steps.expect: Device Tunnel automatically connects at boot — Always On behavior confirmed

sstp_certificate_binding.title: SSTP VPN certificate binding or trust issues — SSL certificate not valid for SSTP

steps.action: netsh http show sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443 — check current SSL certificate binding
steps.expect: Certificate hash displayed. If empty or error, no certificate bound to SSTP

steps.action: Test-NetConnection <VPN server FQDN> -Port 443 — verify TCP 443 reachable
steps.expect: TcpTestSucceeded: True. If false, firewall or network blocking SSTP

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -ProviderName RasClient -MaxEvents 5 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Check for SSTP-specific errors. Common: certificate trust issues, name mismatch

steps.action: certutil -store My — find VPN server certificate thumbprint. Note Subject, Issuer, NotAfter
steps.expect: Certificate present in LocalMachine\My store. Note thumbprint for binding

steps.action: certutil -store My <thumbprint> — verify certificate details. Check CN/SAN matches VPN server FQDN
steps.expect: Certificate CN or SAN contains VPN server FQDN. Name mismatch causes trust failure

steps.action: certutil -verify -urlfetch <certfile> — verify certificate chain and revocation
steps.expect: Certificate chain valid, all certificates in chain trusted. Check for revocation errors

steps.action: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where Subject -like '*<VPN server>*' | Select EnhancedKeyUsageList
steps.expect: EKU includes Server Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1). Required for SSTP SSL

steps.action: On client: check if root CA is in Trusted Root store. certutil -store Root
steps.expect: Issuing CA or root CA present in client's Trusted Root store. Chain trust required

steps.action: Bind correct certificate to SSTP: netsh http add sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443 certhash=<thumbprint> appid={ba195980-cd49-458b-9e23-c84ee0adcd75}
steps.expect: SSL certificate successfully bound. Verify with netsh http show sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443

steps.action: If binding exists but wrong cert: remove first: netsh http delete sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443, then rebind with correct thumbprint
steps.expect: Old binding removed, new correct cert bound. SSTP now uses valid certificate

steps.action: If certificate expired: renew certificate from CA. Request new cert with correct CN/SAN and Server Authentication EKU
steps.expect: New valid certificate issued and installed. Rebind to SSTP with new thumbprint

steps.action: If chain trust issue: export root/intermediate CA certificates and install on client. Import to Trusted Root store (root) and Intermediate store (intermediate)
steps.expect: Full certificate chain present on client. Certificate now trusted

steps.action: Restart RRAS service: Restart-Service RemoteAccess. Restart HTTP service: Restart-Service Http
steps.expect: Services restarted — SSTP uses new certificate binding

steps.action: netsh http show sslcert ipport=0.0.0.0:443 — verify correct certificate bound
steps.expect: Certificate hash matches expected thumbprint. Binding active

steps.action: Test SSTP connection from client: Connect VPN using SSTP protocol
steps.expect: SSTP connection succeeds — no certificate trust errors

steps.action: Verify SSL handshake: use browser or openssl to test SSL to VPN server: openssl s_client -connect <VPN FQDN>:443 -showcerts
steps.expect: SSL handshake successful, certificate chain valid, no trust errors

l2tp_ipsec_mismatch.title: L2TP/IPsec VPN security negotiation failure — Phase 1 or Phase 2 mismatch

steps.action: Test-NetConnection <VPN server FQDN> -Port 500 and -Port 4500. Use portqry for UDP: portqry -n <VPN IP> -e 500 -p udp
steps.expect: UDP 500 and 4500 reachable. Required for IKE and NAT-T

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -ProviderName RasClient -MaxEvents 5 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Error 789 = L2TP security negotiation failed. Check for IPsec phase errors

steps.action: Check if using certificate or PSK: Get-VpnConnection | Select AuthenticationMethod. EAP = cert, MSCHAPv2 = PSK
steps.expect: Authentication method determines troubleshooting path (cert vs PSK)

steps.action: If certificate-based: certutil -store -machine My — verify machine certificate present with IP Security IKE Intermediate EKU
steps.expect: Machine certificate valid with correct EKU (1.3.6.1.5.5.8.2.2). If missing, IPsec fails

steps.action: If PSK-based: check PSK configuration. On RRAS: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\RasMan\Parameters' -Name 'ProhibitIpSec'
steps.expect: PSK configured identically on server and client. Mismatch causes auth failure

steps.action: netsh ipsec dynamic show all — check IPsec security associations and current state
steps.expect: View active SAs. If no SAs, IPsec negotiation failed. Check for mismatched proposals

steps.action: Get-NetIPsecMainModeSA — check Phase 1 (Main Mode) SAs. Get-NetIPsecQuickModeSA — check Phase 2 (Quick Mode) SAs
steps.expect: Main Mode SA present = Phase 1 success. Quick Mode SA present = Phase 2 success. Identify failure point

steps.action: Check NAT-T setting: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\PolicyAgent' -Name AssumeUDPEncapsulationContextOnSendScope
steps.expect: Value 2 = NAT-T enabled for all adapters. Required for clients behind NAT

steps.action: If certificate issue: re-enroll machine certificate with IP Security IKE Intermediate EKU. Ensure CN/SAN matches RRAS server FQDN
steps.expect: Valid machine certificate present. IPsec can negotiate using certificate authentication

steps.action: If PSK mismatch: configure identical PSK on RRAS server and client. On RRAS: Set-VpnServerConfiguration -L2tpPsk <key>. On client: Set-VpnConnection -Name <name> -L2tpPsk <key>
steps.expect: PSK matches on both ends. IPsec authentication succeeds

steps.action: If NAT-T issue: Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\PolicyAgent' -Name AssumeUDPEncapsulationContextOnSendScope -Value 2. Restart RasMan
steps.expect: NAT-T enabled. L2TP works for clients behind NAT devices

steps.action: If IPsec proposal mismatch: adjust encryption/integrity algorithms to match between client and server. Check IPsec policy: Get-NetIPsecPhase1AuthSet; Get-NetIPsecPhase2AuthSet
steps.expect: Proposals match on both ends. IPsec negotiation completes successfully

steps.action: Enable IPsec logging for detailed diagnostics: netsh ipsec set debugmode enable. Reproduce issue, check C:\Windows\debug\ipsec.log
steps.expect: Detailed IPsec negotiation logs show exact failure point. Disable after troubleshooting

steps.action: Retry L2TP/IPsec VPN connection
steps.expect: Connection succeeds — no error 789. Get-VpnConnection shows Connected status

steps.action: Get-NetIPsecMainModeSA | Where RemoteAddress -eq '<client IP>'
steps.expect: Main Mode SA established — Phase 1 (IKE negotiation) successful

steps.action: Get-NetIPsecQuickModeSA | Where RemoteAddress -eq '<client IP>'
steps.expect: Quick Mode SA established — Phase 2 (IPsec tunnel) successful. L2TP traffic now encrypted

nps_radius_misconfiguration.title: NPS RADIUS authentication issues — RADIUS client or policy misconfiguration

steps.action: Test-NetConnection <NPS server> -Port 1812 and -Port 1813 from RRAS server
steps.expect: RADIUS ports accessible — confirms RRAS can reach NPS server

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Id 6273 -MaxEvents 5 on NPS | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Event 6273 shows authentication attempt and rejection reason. Check Reason Code and Failure Reason

steps.action: Get-RemoteAccessRadiusConfiguration on RRAS server | Select ServerName,SharedSecret,AccountingOnOff
steps.expect: RADIUS server configured. Check if accounting enabled and shared secret set

steps.action: netsh nps show client — list all RADIUS clients registered on NPS
steps.expect: RRAS server listed as RADIUS client with correct IP address and shared secret

steps.action: netsh nps show exportedxml — export full NPS configuration. Search for RRAS server entry
steps.expect: RRAS server entry present in RADIUS clients section. Verify IP/FQDN and NAS-Identifier

steps.action: netsh nps show crp — check Connection Request Policy. Ensure it forwards VPN requests to correct Network Policy
steps.expect: Connection Request Policy matches VPN requests. Check Client-IPv4-Address or NAS-IP-Address condition

steps.action: netsh nps show np — check Network Policy. Verify conditions (Windows Groups, NAS-Port-Type, Tunnel-Type) match VPN request
steps.expect: Network Policy has matching conditions. Check Grant Remote Access Permission is enabled

steps.action: Compare shared secret on RRAS and NPS. On RRAS: Get-RemoteAccessRadiusConfiguration. On NPS: netsh nps show client
steps.expect: Shared secret identical on both systems. Mismatch causes authentication failure

steps.action: If RRAS not registered as RADIUS client: add via NPS console or netsh nps add client name=<RRAS> address=<IP> sharedsecret=<secret>
steps.expect: RRAS server registered as RADIUS client. Can now authenticate via NPS

steps.action: If shared secret mismatch: reconfigure on both systems. On RRAS: Set-RemoteAccessRadiusConfiguration -Server <NPS> -SharedSecret <secret>. On NPS: update client secret
steps.expect: Shared secret synchronized. RADIUS authentication now succeeds

steps.action: If Connection Request Policy issue: adjust conditions to match VPN requests. Add Client-IPv4-Address condition for RRAS server IP
steps.expect: CRP matches VPN requests. Requests forwarded to appropriate Network Policy

steps.action: If Network Policy issue: adjust conditions (Windows Groups, NAS-Port-Type=Virtual, Tunnel-Type=IKEv2/SSTP/L2TP). Ensure Grant Remote Access Permission checked
steps.expect: Network Policy matches VPN connection parameters. Authentication granted if credentials valid

steps.action: If RADIUS attributes missing: add standard attributes in Network Policy constraints. Check Framed-Protocol, Service-Type, Tunnel-Type attributes
steps.expect: Required RADIUS attributes present. VPN client receives correct connection parameters

steps.action: Test RADIUS authentication: radclient or similar tool to send test RADIUS request to NPS
steps.expect: RADIUS Access-Accept response received — confirms NPS accepting requests

steps.action: Attempt VPN connection from client
steps.expect: Connection succeeds — NPS authentication successful. No error 691 or 812

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -Id 6272 on NPS | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Event 6272 = authentication succeeded. NPS granted VPN access

steps.action: Get-RemoteAccessConnectionStatistics on RRAS | Select ActiveConnections
steps.expect: Active connection count incremented — confirms NPS authenticated VPN session
